column4: The no-results message renders the raw template placeholder instead of the search term
column5: Loading /products/search/?q=shoes against a running dev server renders the visible text We couldn't find any products matching "{{query}}" - the interpolation placeholder is printed literally rather than substituted. The cause is a variable name mismatch: the locale string at public/locales/en.json:796 is We couldn't find any products matching \"{{query}}\" and expects a variable called query - while the call site at src/pages/products/search/index.tsx:366 passes t("no_products_found_message" - { safeQuery }) which is shorthand for a variable called safeQuery. i18next receives no query key so it leaves the placeholder untouched.
column9: Any search that returns no results - including every search while the catalogue endpoint is failing.
column10: 1. Open /products/search/?q=shoes. 2. Ensure the search returns no results. 3. Read the message under the No products found heading.
column11: The message names the term the customer searched for.
column12: The message shows the literal text {{query}} in quotes.
column13: Every customer who searches for something unavailable sees a broken template string on a high traffic screen - it reads as an unfinished product and gives no confirmation of what was actually searched.
column14: Pass the value under the key the template expects - t("no_products_found_message" - { query: safeQuery }). Check the hi and ar bundles use the same placeholder name.

column4: The categories page subtitle is a truncated sentence
column5: Loading /categories/ renders the heading All Categories followed by the subtitle Discover our complete collection of - the sentence stops mid phrase with no object. The source string is truncated: public/locales/en.json:919 holds "Discover our complete collection of" while its sibling for brands at :909 is complete as "Discover our complete collection of brands". The Arabic bundle carries two matching strings and the Hindi bundle carries none for this phrase so the defect also differs per locale.

column11: A complete sentence naming what the collection contains - matching the brands page wording.
column12: The sentence ends with the word of and no object.

column4: The brands listing renders no empty state and no error state when its fetch fails
column5: Loading /brands/ against a dead catalogue backend renders the page heading and subtitle and then nothing at all before the footer - there is no product or brand grid - no empty state message and no error panel. The equivalent categories page in the same condition does render an empty state reading No Categories Available with an explanatory line and the search page renders its own No products found block. So the blank region is specific to the brands listing rather than a general behaviour. CLAUDE.md section 6.3 requires every screen to ship all four states.
column9: The catalogue endpoint failing or returning no brands.
column10: 1. Make the brands endpoint fail or return an empty set. 2. Open /brands/. 3. Read the area between the subtitle and the footer.
column11: An empty state with a headline and an explanation - or an error state with a retry when the request failed.
column12: The content region is blank with no explanation of any kind.
column13: A customer landing on the brands page during an outage sees an apparently broken page with nothing to act on and no indication whether the catalogue is empty or the request failed.
column14: Add the empty state the categories page already has and an error state with a retry - and take the error from the fetch result so the two cases are distinguishable.

column4: A failed catalogue fetch is presented to the customer as no results rather than an error
column5: With the catalogue backend completely unreachable both /categories/ and /products/search/?q=shoes return HTTP 200 and render their EMPTY states - No Categories Available and No products found respectively - with no indication that anything failed and no retry offered. The customer is told the category list is empty and that their search matched nothing when in fact no request succeeded. This is the observable symptom of code review issue 34 which records the mechanism: the SWR fetcher inside useInfiniteData returns an empty array instead of throwing when a response is unsuccessful so SWR records a success and the hook error is never populated - and the search page does not destructure error at all.
column9: Any failure of the catalogue endpoints - an outage a 500 or a market with no permission to the requested scope.
column10: 1. Make the catalogue endpoints fail. 2. Open /categories/ and then /products/search/?q=shoes. 3. Read what each page tells the customer.
column11: An error state with a retry that is clearly distinct from a genuine no-results outcome.
column12: Both render their empty state as though the catalogue is genuinely empty.
column13: Outages are invisible to customers and to anyone watching the storefront - a failing catalogue looks like missing inventory which suppresses retries and hides the incident. It affects every listing built on the shared infinite data hook.
column14: Throw from the fetcher when a response is unsuccessful so SWR populates error - then surface that error at each consumer and render an error state with retry. Keep the empty state strictly for a successful response with zero items.
